title: Select iso2sd drives by removability, not by /dev/sd name
head: 9af87d80002d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A removable boot device still appears among destructive write targets
leads.consequence: If Omarchy was booted from a USB disk, or its boot NVMe is connected through a hot-pluggable bus, that disk also satisfies the new predicate. It is offered as a target, notwithstanding the description's statement that the boot disk should never appear. Selecting it sends it unchanged to sudo dd; there is no root/boot-device guard before writing. The usual internal fixed SATA disk is excluded, but the claimed protection is conditional.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F6); corroboration; published as Boot disk note (corrected per self-check)

leads.summary: Newly included native SD and hot-pluggable NVMe disks cannot satisfy the unconditional eject
leads.consequence: On a native /dev/mmcblkN SD card, and on an enclosure genuinely exposed via the NVMe driver as /dev/nvmeNnM, successful dd is followed by sudo eject. util-linux eject accepts the removable/hotplug predicate, unmounts partitions and attempts CD-ROM, SCSI, floppy and tape ioctls. The MMC and NVMe drivers do not handle these eject commands, so eject reports 'unable to eject' and iso2sd returns its failure even after the image was written. The resulting status incorrectly implies image creation failed; subsequent invocations may overwrite the same medium again. This is conditional on these newly offered device types actually being present and selectable.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); NVMe ioctl citation verified by coordinator (sol/kernel-7.2-drivers-nvme-host-ioctl.c:580-607) and Opus self-check; published in F2

leads.summary: Help continues recommending /dev/sda as a write target, bypassing the new guard
leads.consequence: When invoked without arguments, the shell prints an example containing /dev/sda, exactly the SATA system disk the PR seeks to remove from the candidate list. An explicit second argument skips lsblk and omarchy-drive-select and is passed directly to sudo dd. This pre-existing override remains intentional, but the displayed example now contradicts the safety rationale and could lead a user to overwrite the system disk. Change the example to an unambiguous placeholder or a removable device and explain that explicit targets are not filtered.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F5); published as Usage example note

leads.summary: An lsblk failure is reported as no removable media, or a partial list is still used
leads.consequence: The producer's exit code is not checked: awk's success masks a failing lsblk, and assigning the pipeline with local masks it again. A failure with empty output produces the reassuring but false 'No removable drives found' message; a producer that emits a candidate then fails can still take the user to a partial picker. On the next run the scan is attempted again, no state persists. Report lsblk failures distinctly and do not present candidates from a failed scan.
leads.triage: factual; masking confirmed but pre-existing (base used the same local x=$(lsblk | grep) shape); not introduced by PR; dropped

leads.summary: The shell functions manual still describes iso2sd as SD-card-only
leads.consequence: Users reading the documented drive-tool list still see an SD-card-only description and no optional output_device parameter, while the picker now offers USB sticks and hot-pluggable enclosures as well. Update the manual's iso2sd entry to describe its wider candidate set and the explicit-device override; the code comment at drives:1 is also stale.
leads.triage: factual; manual/20-shell-functions.md:12 read at head; still accurate ('bootable drive on an SD card ... picking the drive interactively'); low value; dropped

limits: Only synthetic lsblk rows were used in review.py; real block devices, dd, sudo and eject were never executed. The kernel and util-linux control flow establishes the driver ioctl incompatibility, not an observed physical-media run.

Open PR #10716's helper and #12456's loader have separate changed files and both patch onto copies of the head without reject or conflict markers, but their test suites were not run against a merged full checkout; no cross-PR defect is asserted.

flags.claim: A system running from a USB or hot-pluggable disk still has that disk offered, as before.
flags.why: 'as before' holds only for USB (/dev/sd*) boot disks. A system booted from a Thunderbolt/USB4 NVMe drive or an SD card had its boot disk excluded by the base (/dev/sd name filter) and has it offered by this PR (HOTPLUG=1). In the other direction, a USB boot disk with RM=0 on an undescribed port is no longer offered. My own report F6 used the same wording, which contradicts my F1 and my table.

flags.claim: The repository already resolves the disk behind / in omarchy-system-factory-reset
flags.why: omarchy-system-factory-reset resolves the root source device (root_device) and the crypto_LUKS partition behind / (luks_device). It does not resolve the whole disk.

flags.claim: All three rows of the PR's table reproduce, both with a stub lsblk printing those rows and with the real lsblk (util-linux 2.42.3) reading a synthetic sysfs tree.
flags.why: The stub runs reproduced each row separately (Part B). The real-lsblk run used one combined tree with one SATA disk, a USB stick, internal NVMe and an SD card, so it reproduces each device class, not each row. Row 2's two-SATA-disk configuration was never built for real lsblk.

flags.claim: Two isolated runs used synthetic data only: base and head iso2sd with a stub lsblk and stubbed selection and write commands, and the real lsblk against a synthetic sysfs tree (28/28 and 32/32 checks).
flags.why: The wording reads as one run per method. Both runs did both parts, and they also ran the real drive-select/drive-info with stubbed lsblk and gum (Part C). Run 2 is run 1 plus SCSI transport modelling and the TRAN check.

flags.claim: on affected ports, iso2sd image.iso prints "No removable drives found and no drive specified" for a USB drive the base listed.
flags.why: The message appears only when no other drive qualifies. Otherwise the drive is simply missing from the picker.

flags.claim: A disk behind an external hub on a described port is still offered.
flags.why: Lost qualifier: this is true only when firmware describes the port as user-visible (hot-plug). A port described as hard-wired gives the hub "fixed", and the lsblk walk returns 0 at the first "fixed". The synthetic sde case modelled a "removable" port.

flags.claim: For a USB port, the USB core takes it from ACPI port data (_UPC plus _PLD) or a compound hub's DeviceRemovable bits, and otherwise leaves it unknown.
flags.why: Incomplete: the port connect type can also come from devicetree, not only ACPI. On x86 (Omarchy's target) ACPI is the relevant source, so this is a nitpick. My report omitted DT too.

flags.claim: md and dm devices never appear as top-level entries with -d.
flags.why: lsblk skips only devices that have slaves. An md or dm device without slaves (for example a dm zero target, or an md array with no members) is listed. In normal cases its TYPE is not "disk", so the filter still excludes it. My report had the same absolute.

flags.claim: The awk fields cannot shift, because lsblk always prints RM and HOTPLUG as 0/1 and never leaves TYPE empty.
flags.why: 'never leaves TYPE empty' is slightly too absolute: get_type returns an empty string for a dm device whose dm/uuid starts with '-'. That is effectively unreachable, and it does not matter for shifting because TYPE is the last column. The conclusion holds.

flags.claim: This PR makes that target the interactive default.
flags.why: The PR adds the SD card to the interactive picker list. Nothing is preselected; the user picks with gum choose.

flags.claim: USB SSD/HDD enclosures and some flash drives report RM=0.
flags.why: Hardware behaviour, not tested here. The source only shows that RM comes from the SCSI RMB bit. Low risk: this is common knowledge.

flags.claim: AI process: ... Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check ...
flags.why: Model and effort are not in my evidence; the coordinator verifies them with subagents.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new filter does what the description says on current kernels (6.6 or later) and util-linux (2.39 or later). All three rows of the PR's table reproduce with a stub `lsblk` printing those rows. The real `lsblk` (util-linux 2.42.3), reading a synthetic sysfs tree with one device of each class, reports the RM, HOTPLUG and TYPE values the table relies on. The `awk` fields cannot shift: RM and HOTPLUG are always printed as `0`/`1`, and TYPE is the last column. Loop, rom and zram entries are excluded. `omarchy-drive-select` and `omarchy-drive-info` at this head return the picked path for `/dev/sdX`, `/dev/mmcblkN` and `/dev/nvmeXnY` names.

| Device | Base (`/dev/sd` name) | This PR (RM or HOTPLUG) |
|---|---|---|
| Internal SATA disk | offered | not offered |
| Internal NVMe disk | not offered | not offered |
| USB stick (RM=1) | offered | offered |
| SD card in a built-in PCI reader (`/dev/mmcblk0`) | not offered | offered (HOTPLUG=1) |
| Thunderbolt/USB4 NVMe enclosure on an external-facing port | not offered | offered (HOTPLUG=1) |
| USB SSD with RM=0 on a port firmware does not describe | offered | **not offered** (see below) |

Two points are worth a look. Neither changes the verdict on the SATA case the PR targets.

### Some USB disks the base offered are no longer offered

RM comes from the device's own removable bit, and USB SSD/HDD enclosures and some flash drives can report RM=0. For those, only HOTPLUG can keep the disk on the list. Since util-linux 2.39, `lsblk` computes HOTPLUG by walking up sysfs to the first `removable` attribute that reads `removable` or `fixed` (`lib/sysfs.c`), and returns 0 when none is found. The kernel sets that attribute only in the USB core, PCI and MMC code. For a USB port, the USB core takes it from firmware port data (ACPI `_UPC`/`_PLD` on x86) or a compound hub's DeviceRemovable bits, and otherwise leaves it `unknown`. xHCI root hubs are not compound.

```text
USB SSD, RM=0, on a PCIe add-in card port with no ACPI _PLD
  sdd -> usb port "unknown" -> ... -> no "removable"/"fixed" found -> HOTPLUG=0
  lsblk: /dev/sdd 0 0 disk     base: offered     this PR: dropped
```

The same applies to ports firmware marks as hard-wired, to eSATA ports and to hot-swap bay disks: libata sets RM only from the ATA removable bit. A disk behind an external hub on a port firmware describes as user-visible is still offered.

**Impact:** on affected ports, `iso2sd image.iso` leaves out a USB drive the base listed. If nothing else qualifies, it prints "No removable drives found and no drive specified". Passing the device explicitly still works. How common undescribed ports are was not measured.

**Suggested change:** also accept the USB transport. TRAN must be the last column, because it is empty for devices such as zram and loop:

```bash
lsblk -dpno NAME,RM,HOTPLUG,TYPE,TRAN |
  awk '$4 == "disk" && ($2 == 1 || $3 == 1 || $5 == "usb") { print $1 }'
```

In the synthetic sysfs run, this adds exactly `/dev/sdd` to the PR's list and nothing else. The trade-off: it offers every USB-attached disk again, as the base did, including a USB boot disk.

### `eject` fails after writing to the newly offered SD and NVMe targets

`iso2sd` still ends with `sudo eject "$drive"`. util-linux `eject` accepts these devices, since its check is the same RM-or-HOTPLUG test. It then tries only CD-ROM, SCSI (SG_IO), floppy and tape eject ioctls (`sys-utils/eject.c`). The MMC block driver returns `-EINVAL` for anything but its own `MMC_IOC_*` commands (`drivers/mmc/core/block.c`), and the NVMe namespace ioctl handler returns `-ENOTTY` for anything outside its NVMe command set (`drivers/nvme/host/ioctl.c`).

**Impact:** after `dd` has written the image to an SD card in a built-in reader (the table's third row), the user sees `eject: unable to eject`, and `iso2sd` returns a failure status even though the write finished. Explicit `/dev/mmcblk*` arguments already behaved this way. This PR adds those targets to the interactive picker. This comes from source reading only; `eject` was not run.

**Suggested change:** check the status of `dd` (which `iso2sd` does not do today), and after a successful write treat an `eject` failure as non-fatal or skip `eject` for `mmcblk` and `nvme` targets. A bare `sudo eject "$drive" || true` would also hide an `eject` error after a failed `dd`.

**Minor notes:**

- **Empty card readers:** `lsblk` lists zero-size devices unless given `-A`/`--noempty`. An empty slot in a built-in USB card reader that shows up as a 0B disk with RM=1 passes the new filter, as it passed the old one, so "No removable drives found" never appears on such laptops. Adding `-A` drops the empty slot (checked in the synthetic run).
- **Comment wording:** ordinary USB NVMe enclosures (UAS bridges) appear as `/dev/sdX` and were already matched. Only Thunderbolt/USB4 enclosures appear as `/dev/nvme*`, so "USB enclosures that present as NVMe" in the new code comment could name those instead.
- **Usage example:** `drives:5` still suggests `iso2sd ... /dev/sda`, which the PR describes as the system disk on SATA machines. An explicit device skips the new filter and goes straight to `dd`.
- **Boot disk:** removability is not the same as "not the boot disk". A system running from a USB disk still has that disk offered, as before, and one running from a Thunderbolt/USB4 NVMe drive or an SD card now has it offered. Excluding the disk that backs `/` would be a stronger guard.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head against util-linux v2.42.4 and Linux v7.2 (v6.5/v6.6 compared for the MMC change). Two isolated runs used synthetic data only (28/28 and 32/32 checks). Each ran base and head `iso2sd` with a stub `lsblk` and stubbed selection and write commands, the real `lsblk` against a synthetic sysfs tree, and the real selection helpers; the second added the TRAN variant. No real block devices were queried or written, and `dd` and `eject` were not run. The `eject` finding comes from source reading. Related open PRs #12717 (same file, `format-drive` only) and #10716 (`omarchy-drive-select` input handling) do not conflict with this change.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
